subject: Dedicated slab orbit & fallback routing for OrbitalAI — sizing and burst policy
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@orbitalai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orbitalai.com
Date: 2029-03-13T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity questions — weekend batch + peak inference bursts

Hi Mina / Karthik,

Thanks for taking this call last week. We're sizing Dedicated capacity for OrbitalAI and need to understand how Redwood would handle our typical workload profile:

- Baseline steady-state inference: ~200 qps (95ms p95 target) for synchronous customers during business hours.
- Daily peak windows (evening peak + nightly batch overlap): short spikes up to ~1,500 qps lasting ~2–3 hours.
- Heavy batch jobs (offline training/embedding) that can be scheduled and tolerate preemption.

Questions:
1) What are recommended baseline slab sizes to meet the 95ms p95 target without sustained overprovisioning?
2) How does Redwood's autoscale + burst system handle short high-volume spikes — pre-warmed shoulder pools, ephemeral slabs, or fallback routing to hosted variants?
3) Can we set a negotiated 'burst credit bank' for predictable billing during peaks, and how would evictions/preemption be signaled?

Can you send a short mutual action plan and a rough cost model (GPU counts, expected reserved + ephemeral spend)? If helpful, I've attached a traffic snapshot and can share a fuller trace for profiling.

Thanks,

Elena Park
VP Engineering, OrbitalAI
(elena.park@orbitalai.com)

Attachments: orbitalai-traffic-snapshot.json (traffic sample)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@orbitalai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-14T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questions — weekend batch + peak inference bursts

Hi Elena — thanks for the snapshot, this is exactly the sort of detail we need.

Quick summary of our recommended approach based on the profile you sent:

- Baseline slab: a dedicated pool sized to handle ~220–250 qps with 20% headroom. For your model and latency target that maps to ~28–36 GPUs (A100 80GB equivalents); if you opt for H100 that number drops ~15–20%.

- Burst strategy (what we call the "orbit" pattern):
  * Shoulder pool: a small always-on reserve (5–8 GPUs) kept warm to absorb immediate spikes while autoscale provisions ephemeral capacity.
  * Ephemeral slabs: short-lived instances (preemptible or reserved on-demand) provisioned automatically up to a configurable max (we recommend up to 1.8–2x baseline for your peak profile).
  * Fallback routing: when ephemeral provisioning hits the cap, traffic can be routed to a quantized, lower-cost hosted model variant (same model family, mixed-quant) with an attached SLO downgrade notice.

- Autoscale behavior and signals:
  * Provisioning ramp: scale decisions are driven by rolling qps and i-cache/KV hit rates; typical spin-up for ephemerals is ~45–120s depending on region and GPU type.
  * Eviction policy: preemptible ephemerals receive a 90s graceful drain; we stream tokens to clients while draining and failover to fallback variant if necessary.

- Billing / Burst credits:
  * We can structure a burst credit bank that offsets ephemeral consumption up to an agreed monthly cap; overages billed at on-demand rates.

Next steps:
- We'll run a short profiler (1–2 hour replay) against a staging slab to produce a capacity model and a cost estimate (see attached rdwd_capacity_model_v1.xlsx).
- Suggest a 45-minute follow-up with our SRE (Rishi) and your platform lead to review eviction windows and canary rollout policies. Proposed times: Thu 3/21 or Mon 3/25.

I've attached a draft SLA addendum for burst terms (sla-burst-term-draft.pdf).

Best,

Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Attachments: rdwd_capacity_model_v1.xlsx, sla-burst-term-draft.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-03-14T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questions — technical notes on eviction and fallback

Mina / team,

Couple of technical notes to fold into the proposal before we share with Orbital:

- Eviction windows: 90s drain is reasonable; increase to 120s if we expect large request sizes or long streaming sessions. Add explicit 'drain_announce' webhook so customers' clients can backoff gracefully.

- Max preemptible share: recommend limiting ephemerals to 40% of total burst capacity in regionally constrained clusters to reduce noisy neighbor risk.

- Fallback variant behavior: include an automatic 'explain' header in responses when routed to fallback (so product teams can surface temporary quality deltas), and record these at token granularity for regressions.

- Canary plan: canary traffic should test both scale-up and scale-down paths; suggest 10% traffic for first 24h then 25% for next 72h before full cutover.

I'll update the capacity workbook with a sheet showing cost sensitivity to preemptible ratio and send back.

-r

Rishi Malhotra
SRE, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
